articles.title: I thought then that Sachin didn’t help: When Cricketer Vinod Kambli said this and his latest video from elder care centre tugs the heart
articles.summary: For a cricketer once known for the effortless strokeplay that made him one of India’s most talked-about batting talents, Vinod Kambli’s latest video has
articles.body: For a cricketer once known for the effortless strokeplay that made him one of India’s most talked-about batting talents, Vinod Kambli’s latest video has left fans looking at a very different chapter of his life.A video of the former India batter at an elderly-care centre in Thane has surfaced on social media, showing Kambli speaking about the care he is receiving there. He appears to struggle while speaking in parts of the short clip, prompting fresh concern among fans about his health.Kambli himself, however, speaks positively about the place. Introducing himself in the video, he says he has received affection and does not feel as though he is away from home. He also praises the facilities and cleanliness at the centre.“I am Vinod Kambli. I have received a lot of love. And as for all the people who are here, it doesn't feel anywhere here like I am not at home,” he says in the video. He also describes the facilities and hygiene as “absolutely top-class” and identifies the place as Nidan. The video was shared on social media on September 25.A health battle that has continued for yearsThe latest video comes after a series of health concerns surrounding Kambli over the past few years. In December 2024, Kambli was hospitalised in Thane after suffering from a urinary tract infection and low blood pressure. Doctors also found electrolyte abnormalities that were affecting his muscles and movement, along with old blood clots in his brain linked to an earlier stroke. He was discharged in January 2025 after roughly two weeks of treatment.Kambli had spoken about his health himself around that period. In an interview with The Times of India in December 2024, he said he was ready to enter rehabilitation and also spoke about the support he had received from childhood friend Sachin Tendulkar.“At that time, it came to my mind that Sachin didn't help. I was extremely frustrated. But Sachin did everything for me, including paying for my two surgeries in 2013,” Kambli had said.He also recalled his cricketing journey and the repeated comebacks he had made during his career. “Sachin told me how to play. I made nine comebacks. We are cricketers; we get hurt. When we get out, we also get hurt,” he said.Months earlier, after another video of Kambli struggling to walk went viral, he had himself sought to reassure friends and fans. Speaking to close friends who visited him at home in August 2024, Kambli said: “I'm good,” before adding, “By the grace of God, I'm surviving. I'm fit and fine. I'm ready to bat at No 3.”From schoolboy sensation to India batterKambli’s story is inseparable from that of Tendulkar. The two were childhood friends and became famous after their unbeaten 664-run partnership for Shardashram Vidyamandir in a school match in 1988.Kambli went on to make his India debut in 1991 and established himself as a gifted left-handed batter. He played 17 Tests, scoring 1,084 runs at an average of 54.20 with four centuries. In 104 ODIs, he scored 2,477 runs.His Test career included a memorable run of form in the early 1990s. He became the first Indian to score back-to-back Test double centuries, making 224 against England at Wankhede Stadium in 1993 and 227 against Zimbabwe at Delhi in 1994.Looking back at the innings that meant the most to him, Kambli said in December 2024: “The double hundred at Wankhede, I will cherish the most. Achrekar sir was with me, and we had such a great team.”For fans who remember Kambli primarily through those innings, the latest video is a stark reminder of how dramatically life can change after a sporting career ends.Yet Kambli’s own message from the care centre is not one of complaint. He talks about being cared for, receiving affection and feeling at home. As concern around his health grows again, those are also the words he has chosen to leave with the people watching him now.Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. articles.title: ‘No jealousy’: Dhruv Jurel reveals what Vaibhav Sooryavanshi does that others ‘can’t even dream of’
articles.summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi may not yet be a guaranteed name in India’s Playing XI, but at just 15, the teenager has already grown into a phenomenon that extends
articles.body: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi may not yet be a guaranteed name in India’s Playing XI, but at just 15, the teenager has already grown into a phenomenon that extends far beyond Indian cricket.In barely two years, Sooryavanshi has turned himself into a national sensation and, increasingly, a global sporting attraction. Among 15-year-old athletes, only Lamine Yamal can claim a larger following, largely because of football’s worldwide reach. In cricket, however, Sooryavanshi’s popularity stands in a league of its own.The teenager has already shared the dressing room with several members of India’s T20 World Cup-winning side, while his rapid rise has inevitably raised questions about competition for places.Sanju Samson could be viewed as Sooryavanshi’s most direct competition, but Dhruv Jurel, who has captained the youngster and is himself making a mark in Test cricket, sees little point in comparing the two.For Jurel, comparisons only make sense when players possess similar skill sets. Sooryavanshi, in his view, is operating at a level that is difficult to even comprehend.“He deserves all the praise. What he does is something you can’t even dream of. A 15-year-old kid smashing everybody. It’s just WOW. Honestly, there’s no jealousy. There’s no comparison either. What is there to compare? It’s beyond comprehension. Comparisons happen when you think you can do something similar. He is too good. An unbelievable kid. We watch in awe, and he makes life easier for us as batters. In the Powerplay, he keeps smashing, and watching him, you feel that if we get a chance, we should also start hitting, because he just keeps smashing,” Jurel told Aakash Chopra on the former India opener’s podcast.Jurel is also enjoying a prolific run himself. He recently ended the series as India’s second-highest run-scorer behind Devdutt Padikkal and third-highest overall, accumulating 173 runs.His tally included one fifty and a hundred, Initially, Jurel was fighting for a spot with Pant in the Test playing XI, but later the management chose to play him as a specialist batter.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Rajasthan cricket elections: Five political scions enter fray for RCA president’s post
articles.summary: Jaipur: Five sons of prominent politicians filed their nominations on Saturday, the final day of the submission window for the Rajasthan Cricket
articles.body: Jaipur: Five sons of prominent politicians filed their nominations on Saturday, the final day of the submission window for the Rajasthan Cricket Association (RCA) executive elections, setting up a heavily contested battle for control of the sports body. Amid intense political maneuvering, over 20 District Cricket Association (DCA) secretaries have reportedly been moved to resort-style retreats as district secretaries hold key voting power and are pushing for a 4-2 power-sharing compromise, letting the BJP high command dictate the top two posts while reserving the remaining four positions for district representatives.Jodhpur DCA president Dhananjai Singh Khimsar, son of current health minister Gajendra Singh Khimsar, and Churu DCA president Parakram Singh Rathore, son of former Leader of Opposition Rajendra Singh Rathore, both submitted their papers for the apex post of president. Their bids anchor a five-way presidential race that also includes former ad hoc panel convener DD Kumawat, Rajesh Saraswat and Brij Kishore Upadhyay.Meanwhile, the strategic inclusion of three newly affiliated district associations could prove decisive in the final outcome, provided the elections proceed past high command consensus.A similar convergence of political family members defines the races for the remaining executive roles. Education minister Madan Dilawar’s son Pawan Dilawar, filed his nomination for the vice-president post. He faces competition from Alwar DCA president Mohit Yadav, son of BJP MLA Dr Jaswant Singh Yadav, who is double-filing for both vice-president and secretary.The secretarial contest also features Ashish Tiwari, son of Rajya Sabha MP Ghanshyam Tiwari, who has simultaneously staked a claim for the treasurer’s role. Joining them in the multi-cornered race for secretary are Pinkesh Kumar Jain, Sumendra Tiwari, Manoj Kumar Sharma and Upadhyay.The financial and operational portfolios are equally competitive. Vying alongside Ashish Tiwari for the treasurer position are Pinkesh Kumar Jain, Vishnu Prakash Agarwal, Sushil Jain, and Rajesh Kumar Mathur. Meanwhile, the joint secretary portfolio has drawn entries from Govind Swaroop Upadhyay, Vinod Saharan, Ratan Singh Shekhawat, Sushil Jain, and Rajesh Saraswat.Amid the field of political heavyweights, the election features Dausa DCA president Shobhana Gurjar, a national-level shooter and veteran sports administrator, who filed her papers for executive committee member. She faces a multi-cornered contest against Rajesh Choudhary, Dharmveer Singh Shekhawat, and Arisht Singhvi.The administrative roadmap now moves into its final phases at the RCA Academy. Election authorities will conduct the official scrutiny of all submitted papers on Sunday (September 27), followed by the candidate withdrawal window on Monday (September 28), leading up to voting and results on Tuesday (September 29).Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Virat Kohli on the brink of history, 59 runs away from breaking Sachin Tendulkar's ODI record
articles.summary: Virat Kohli is once again on the cusp of an ODI milestone that would add another remarkable chapter to his extraordinary career.
articles.body: Virat Kohli is once again on the cusp of an ODI milestone that would add another remarkable chapter to his extraordinary career. The former India captain needs just 59 runs in the opening ODI against West Indies in Thiruvananthapuram on Sunday to become only the second batter in men's ODI history to reach the 15,000-run mark, joining Sachin Tendulkar in an exclusive club.Kohli has accumulated 14,941 runs in 314 ODIs and 302 innings at an average of 58.59, with 54 centuries and 79 fifties. Tendulkar remains the format's leading run-scorer with 18,426 runs, meaning Kohli's next landmark will place him alongside the player whose ODI records have defined Indian cricket for decades.But the 15,000-run mark is only one of several records within Kohli's reach.Kohli set to rewrite fastest-to-15,000 recordIf Kohli scores the required 59 runs against West Indies, he will reach 15,000 ODI runs in his 303rd innings. That would make him the fastest batter to the landmark by a considerable margin. Tendulkar reached 15,000 runs in his 377th ODI innings in 2007. Kohli would therefore get there 74 innings earlier than his illustrious predecessor.The landmark would also fit into a pattern that has followed Kohli throughout his ODI career. He became the fastest batter to 13,000 ODI runs when he reached the mark in 267 innings in 2023, breaking Tendulkar's previous record of 321 innings.West Indies have been one of Kohli's favourite opponentsThere is another layer to the milestone given the opposition. Kohli has enjoyed remarkable success against West Indies, scoring 2,261 runs in 43 matches and 41 innings at an average of 66.50. He has nine centuries and 11 fifties against them.Thiruvananthapuram has also been a productive venue for the right-hander. He has scored 199 runs without being dismissed in two ODIs at the venue, including his sensational unbeaten 166 against Sri Lanka in January 2023.Tendulkar's home record also within touching distanceKohli has another Tendulkar record in his sights, the most ODI runs scored in home conditions. Tendulkar amassed 6,976 ODI runs in India. Kohli currently has 6,867, leaving him 110 runs short of overtaking the former India opener.Kohli's home ODI numbers underline his consistency. He has scored those 6,867 runs in 130 matches and 127 innings, averaging 62.42, with 27 centuries and 36 fifties.Kohli's pursuit of Tendulkar's records extends beyond ODIs. The former India captain currently has 85 international centuries and remains on the path towards the 100-century landmark that Tendulkar was the first to reach.At home, Kohli has 41 international hundreds, with Tendulkar's record standing at 42. Two more centuries in India would take Kohli past his former teammate and India's batting icon in that particular category.Kohli is also closing in on Tendulkar's record for most List-A centuries. Kohli has 59 List-A hundreds, while Tendulkar finished his career with 60. Since List-A cricket includes ODIs as well as other recognised 50-over matches, Kohli needs two more hundreds to move clear of Tendulkar at the top of the Indian list.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India vs West Indies Live Score, 1st ODI: Shubman Gill wins toss as India opt to field first; Naman Dhir make
articles.body: IND vs WI Live Score: India have luxury of experimenting, West Indies don't The first ODI presents two very different situations for India and West Indies. India, ranked ten places above West Indies in the ODI standings, can afford to test their backups, make changes and explore combinations while still giving their leading players much-needed match practice before the World Cup. West Indies have no such luxury in terms of qualification. Their hopes of automatically making the World Cup are over, meaning they will have to take the Qualifier route five months from now. That makes the India series an important measuring stick. Daren Sammy has called it a great opportunity to challenge and assess the team in ODIs, while Shai Hope acknowledged that facing India in their backyard would be a tough uphill battle..India vs West Indies Live: What makes India vs West Indies opener intriguing India and West Indies bring contrasting storylines into their first ODI in Thiruvananthapuram. India are looking towards a World Cup a year away, with selection questions around No.4 and their pace combination. Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma remain central figures, while Shubman Gill's brief injury scare added another talking point before the opener. West Indies are entering a rebuilding phase after missing automatic World Cup qualification. Their last bilateral ODI series win over India came in 2006, and India have won all 13 series between the sides since. Shai Hope remains their key batting figure, while the return of Jewel Andrew and the presence of Amir Jangoo add intrigue. The opener therefore offers India a chance to build and West Indies a chance to test themselves..IND vs WI Live Score: West Indies attack has plenty of variety West Indies enter the ODI series with several different bowling options at their disposal. Matthew Forde and Jayden Seales can provide swing and seam, while Alzarri Joseph offers a threat during the middle overs. Vitel Lawes adds another dimension to the attack. The side does not have the same left-arm pace option, but there is still considerable depth across the bowling group. Gudakesh Motie brings spin into the equation, while the team must also decide between Jayden Seales and Shamar Joseph for one place in the probable XI. Against an Indian batting line-up that has averaged 39.25 runs per wicket since the last World Cup, West Indies' variety will be tested from the outset..India vs West Indies Live: West Indies need to improve against spin West Indies' numbers against spin provide an obvious area for improvement ahead of their India challenge. Since the end of the last World Cup, they have averaged 28.09 against spin, better than only Zimbabwe among the traditional ODI teams. That record becomes especially relevant against an Indian attack featuring Ravindra Jadeja and Kuldeep Yadav. Jadeja rarely gives batters easy scoring opportunities, while Kuldeep provides a different threat through his wicket-taking ability. West Indies will need their batters to find a way through that challenge if they are to compete against India's strong top order. Their ability to counter spin could shape the outcome of the three-match series..IND vs WI Live Score: Greenfield Stadium could offer seamers a say The Greenfield International Stadium has hosted only two previous ODIs, but its limited history still offers an interesting clue for the opening match. The venue has the third-best bowling average for seamers among grounds in India, with seamers averaging 25.35. That could bring India's and West Indies' pace attacks into focus. West Indies have several options capable of exploiting movement, with Matthew Forde and Jayden Seales offering swing and seam, Alzarri Joseph providing a middle-overs threat and Vitel Lawes adding an X-factor. There is also minimal threat of rain in Thiruvananthapuram on Sunday, leaving the quicks to make the most of the conditions available..IND vs WI Live Score: Nitish Reddy could have a bigger bowling role Nitish Kumar Reddy could be asked to shoulder a much bigger bowling workload when India face West Indies. With Hardik Pandya and Jasprit Bumrah absent from the ODI squad, India are short of both allround balance and fast-bowling depth. Reddy, who has only recently returned to full fitness himself, could be required to bowl his complete quota of 10 overs. That would represent a significant responsibility for the young allrounder. Morne Morkel has already indicated that Reddy can compete for the allrounder's spot, while India's team combination could depend on how much bowling they believe they can get from him. His role could influence the balance of the XI..India vs West Indies Live: John Campbell set to return at the top John Campbell is in line to return to the top of the West Indies batting order for the first ODI against India. Campbell has returned after surgery and is expected to reclaim his opening position. Justin Greaves could partner him, having stepped in for Campbell during two of West Indies' five ODIs against New Zealand in July. The opening combination will be important against an India attack that could include Mohammed Siraj, Prasidh Krishna and Kuldeep Yadav. West Indies have struggled for consistency at the top, with their top three averaging 29.35 since the end of the last World Cup. Campbell's return gives the visitors another chance to strengthen that department..India vs West Indies Live: Shubman Gill scare adds another subplot for India India briefly had an injury scare ahead of the first ODI when captain Shubman Gill was struck on the elbow by a Mohammed Siraj delivery during practice. Gill left the nets and spent the rest of the session with an icepack on the affected area. He did not return to bat that day, raising concerns about his availability for the series opener. However, Sitanshu Kotak subsequently indicated that Gill would be good to play. India do have cover if there is a late change, with Yashasvi Jaiswal waiting for an opportunity at the top of the order. For now, the expectation is that Gill will lead India against West Indies, with Rohit Sharma likely to partner him at the top..IND vs WI Live Score: West Indies have a new challenge with Rutherford absent West Indies will begin the ODI series without Sherfane Rutherford, who is set to miss the opening match because of a personal matter. According to Cricket West Indies, Rutherford is expected to join the squad before the second ODI. His absence could open the door for Amir Jangoo, who is in line for an opportunity in the opening game. Jangoo is part of a West Indies side combining established names with players still building their international careers. The visitors will also have to decide on their bowling combination, with Jayden Seales and Shamar Joseph competing for one position in the probable XI. The opening match could therefore provide opportunities for players outside the regular combination..India vs West Indies Live: India have been among ODI cricket's fastest scorers India's approach with the bat has been one of the notable features of their ODI cricket since the last World Cup. They have scored at 6.08 runs per over during this period, the second-highest rate among teams, behind England's 6.17. India have managed to maintain that scoring speed while averaging 39.25 runs per wicket. The numbers underline the balance between aggression and consistency that India have brought to the format. Virat Kohli's recent strike-rate surge adds another dimension to that approach. He has scored at 106.66 in ODIs in 2026, suggesting India's batting tempo could remain an important talking point during the West Indies series..India vs West Indies Live: Weather, humidity and new-ball challenge in focus Weather conditions could add another element to the opening ODI between India and West Indies in Thiruvananthapuram. The weather remained largely clear in the two days leading into the match, although a brief but sharp spell of rain arrived around an hour before India's practice on September 25. The day before the opener remained hot and humid, with the India team opting out of practice apart from Auqib Nabi's batting stint. Morne Morkel described the conditions as good for batting, although he felt the new-ball phase could be a little challenging based on feedback from India's batters. West Indies also trained, though their session was not conducted at full intensity..IND vs WI 1st ODI: India's top order brings contrasting numbers India's top three have been among their strongest performers since the end of the last World Cup. The top three have averaged 53.34 during that period, highlighting the consistency available at the top of India's batting order. West Indies, by comparison, have a corresponding top-three average of 29.35. The difference is significant, but West Indies have their own standout performer in the middle order. Shai Hope has scored 1,350 runs since the end of the last World Cup, averaging 50 at a strike rate of 92.91. The series therefore pits India's high-performing top order against a West Indies batting line-up looking to build around Hope..IND vs WI Live: West Indies face a spin challenge in Thiruvananthapuram West Indies could face a major test against India's spinners in Thiruvananthapuram. Since the end of the last World Cup, West Indies have averaged only 28.09 against spin. Among the traditional ODI teams, only Zimbabwe have a lower average during that period. That makes the presence of Ravindra Jadeja and Kuldeep Yadav particularly significant. Jadeja is known for keeping batters under pressure, while Kuldeep offers a wicket-taking threat. The venue has also previously produced problems for West Indies. When the teams met here in 2018, West Indies were bowled out for 104, with Jadeja claiming four wickets. How West Indies handle India's spin could become a major factor..IND vs WI 1st ODI: Alzarri Joseph returns after CPL triumph Alzarri Joseph enters the India series with momentum after helping Antigua and Barbuda Falcons win the CPL title. His return is another important development for West Indies, particularly after the fast bowler and head coach Daren Sammy had a public disagreement earlier this year. Joseph has made it clear that his focus remains on representing West Indies, regardless of his relationship with the coach. Sammy has also highlighted Joseph's return to the team at the start of the ODI series. For West Indies, Joseph provides a threat through the middle overs and adds experience to an attack that also includes Matthew Forde, Jayden Seales and Vitel Lawes..IND vs WI Live Score: Virat Kohli closes in on 15,000 ODI runs Virat Kohli could reach another major ODI milestone when India face West Indies in Thiruvananthapuram. Kohli is just 59 runs away from completing 15,000 ODI runs. His record against West Indies makes the possibility particularly intriguing, with the former India captain averaging 66.50 against them. Kohli has also been scoring at a faster rate in 2026. Across six matches this year, he has a strike rate of 106.66, a significant shift from his traditionally measured approach in the format. The only other year when Kohli finished an ODI calendar year with a strike rate above 100 was 2018. A milestone could therefore add another subplot to Sunday's opener..India vs West Indies Live Score: India still searching for first-choice ODI combination India's ODI preparations for the 2027 World Cup continue with another series where their first-choice combination remains unavailable. India have played three ODI series this year and lost two, with injuries and their focus on the T20 World Cup affecting their ability to field their strongest side. For the West Indies series, Hardik Pandya and Jasprit Bumrah are again absent. Their absence leaves India short of the allround balance and fast-bowling quality they bring to the XI. Nitish Kumar Reddy could therefore have a bigger role with the ball, potentially bowling his full quota of 10 overs. India will be looking to use the series to find solutions before the World Cup.

articles.title: 'I was distraught': Virat Kohli reveals defeat that was 'too tough to swallow'
articles.summary: India's recent ICC success may have brought an end to their long-standing trophy drought, but some World Cup defeats continue to remain difficult memories
articles.body: India's recent ICC success may have brought an end to their long-standing trophy drought, but some World Cup defeats continue to remain difficult memories for Virat Kohli.India won back-to-back T20 World Cup titles before adding the Champions Trophy, but the heartbreak of November 19, 2023 still remains fresh in the minds of ardent cricket followers. Rohit Sharma has spoken about that defeat on several occasions.For Kohli, though, the 2019 World Cup semifinal loss to New Zealand remains an even more painful experience.'2019 was a jolt for us'The semifinal in Manchester stretched across two days after persistent rain interrupted New Zealand's innings in the 47th over. The Black Caps returned the following day to finish on 239/8 before India fell 18 runs short in the chase.The match is particularly remembered for MS Dhoni's heartbreaking run-out by Martin Guptill in the 49th over.Bhuvneshwar Kumar, who took three wickets in the game, recently described the defeat as "heartbreaking". Kohli agreed with his former India team-mate, admitting that the loss left him distraught.“Playing Australia in the 2015 semifinal, you are very well aware of your strength and weaknesses and Australia is always difficult. We always knew that if it gets to a massive score, it will be tough, and that is what happened. They were phenomenal.“But 2019 was a jolt for us. 240... it rained out. Had we played that day, things would have been different. But next morning, fresh new ball attack. They got the best of the conditions and they put us under attack and they banked on the hesitation that we had.“That was too tough to swallow and process. I was distraught. After that I was totally gone mentally for a couple of months,” he told JioStar ahead of India’s first ODI against West Indies.Kohli remembers 2023 dressing-room atmosphereKohli viewed India's run to the 2023 World Cup final differently, describing the campaign as a "massive step forward" in terms of both talent and performance.More than the results, however, he remembered the atmosphere within the squad and the way the players responded to setbacks.“That whole World Cup was great, the environment was phenomenal. Within the team, you could see the camaraderie; everyone was happy playing for each other.“Even losing someone like Hardik early on, we never spoke about what would happen next although it was a big loss in terms of what he brings. But, Shami came and you know what he can do.“So, everyone had a feeling that it was our World Cup,” he added.'I feel the same about the World Cup final'India's campaign ultimately ended with a defeat to Australia in the final in Ahmedabad, another result that Kohli found difficult to process.He compared the feeling to the flashbacks he experienced after the 2016 IPL final, which continued until Royal Challengers Bengaluru won the IPL in 2025.“Before we won the IPL in 2025, I used to get flashbacks of the 2016 final. I feel the same about the World Cup final as well.“I was playing on 54 and had set myself up for a big hundred; like, if I got 140-150, we would be in a great position to win that game.“But as soon as I played on, it was very tough to process for many days. And you keep thinking about it.”Kohli's unfinished World Cup businessDespite the painful memories, Kohli does not believe his World Cup journey is complete.“The thought will never cross my mind that the business I had is finished. As long as you’re playing, there is always something to look forward to. And I’m looking forward to the World Cup, looking at what lies ahead for me.“When the World Cup is played, when we play an ICC tournament, it has its own unique challenge, because you face different opponents, you play at different venues.“So, you have to prepare differently, think in a different way and that is the challenge,” he said.Kohli has confirmed that the 2027 ICC tournament will be his last World Cup for India. That decision has given his next campaign an added significance.“For me, it’s the last World Cup I’m going to play for India. And that is my motivation,” he added.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: How Hayden Wesneski's 'incredible' effort saved Houston Astros' bullpen for season-defining finale
articles.summary: With Houston desperate for an effective start, Hayden Wesneski gave more than that, providing length to preserve the Astros' relief corps for Sunday's AL Wes...
articles.body:
WEST SACRAMENTO, Calif. - Efficiency was not Hayden Wesneski 's primary goal Saturday. Effectiveness was. That he provided both put the Houston Astros in the best position they could reasonably ask going into a game 162 that will define their season.

Wesneski, the right-hander making his 11th start back from elbow surgery, worked seven strong innings in a 13-2 blowout of the A's that allowed the Astros to rest their beleaguered bullpen ahead of Sunday, when the American League West race will be decided.

The Astros and Rangers will enter the final day of the season tied atop the AL West at 80-81. The Astros hold the tiebreaker and can clinch the division with either a win or a Texas loss against the Twins. Both games will start shortly after 2 p.m. CT.

The Astros will start Peter Lambert , who will be on two days' rest after throwing 62 pitches across 2 ⅔ innings in the series opener against the A's at Sutter Health Park. The short rest will likely create a short leash for Lambert.

"We're going to need someone to start the game and give us a couple innings trying to get to the back end" of the bullpen, manager Joe Espada said, before the Astros announced Lambert will start.

That the Astros figure to rely heavily on their bullpen Sunday underscored the magnitude of Wesneski's outing Saturday night.

Prior to Friday, when Hunter Brown threw 5 ⅓ innings , Houston 's starter had not completed the third inning in its previous three games. Astros relievers combined to work 20 innings in that stretch.

Entering Saturday, AJ Blubaugh , Bennett Sousa and Logan VanWey had all pitched three of the past four days. Miguel Ullola was one day removed from throwing 35 pitches. Bryan Abreu had pitched back-to-back days Wednesday and Thursday. Closer Josh Hader had not pitched since throwing 44 pitches , his most in a regular-season game since 2019, on Wednesday in Seattle .

Due to Wesneski holding the A's to two runs over seven innings Saturday, and their offense erupting for 16 hits and five home runs behind him, the Astros were able to use Ronel Blanco to work the final two innings of a critical victory and preserve the rest of their bullpen arms for Sunday. Hader and Abreu will both be on multiple days' rest, perhaps expanding their usage potential in a must-win game.

"Amazing job," shortstop Jeremy Peña said of Wesneski. "He went above and beyond today. He saved our bullpen. Everyone's fresh for tomorrow."

Wesneski had a string of less efficient outings in late August. Yet Saturday marked the fifth time he has completed at least six innings in 11 starts since returning from elbow surgery. He has completed seven innings in three of those starts.

"That (depth) wasn't the goal, the goal was to give us a good quality start just like always and to win the game," Wesneski said. "You don't put too much pressure on yourself to have to go nine today, that's too much. We need to get through the first and then give our team a chance to win the game."

The A's lineup is missing some of its best hitters to injury, yet it scored four runs against Lambert in his 2 ⅔ innings Thursday and made Brown throw 100 pitches in his 5 ⅓ innings Friday. Wesneski had a larger lead to work with in his later innings, but he was economical before Houston built it.

Wesneski recorded his first nine outs on 20 pitches. He worked his second and third innings on just five pitches each, inducing double plays to end them. The fast start not only set a tone for his night but got Houston's offense back to the plate at the A's hitter-friendly minor-league ballpark.

"Strikes," Espada said. "He threw a ton of strikes. And every time he got some guys on base, he got the ground ball."

Houston's inability to turn a double play in the fourth - with Peña bobbling a ground ball and making a wide throw to first base on another - contributed a 21-pitch inning for Wesneski. One run scored, but Wesneski induced a ground out from Donovan Walton to strand runners at first and third.

The A's did not put another runner in scoring position until the seventh inning. By that point, the Astros had built an eight-run lead. Wesneski threw 71% strikes and first-pitch strikes to 21 of 27 batters faced. He issued just one walk and struck out five. He generated 10 outs via ground ball.

"Huge by him," slugger Yordan Alvarez said, through an interpreter. "It's an incredible thing that he did there. And to be able to give the bullpen a day off, it's very important for the game tomorrow."

Wesneski, who made his season debut July 29, posted a 3.25 ERA over his 61 innings. The Astros went 8-3 in games he started, illustrating his importance if they do reach the postseason.

After a trade deadline at which the Astros did not acquire pitching, former general manager Dana Brown expressed optimism that Wesneski and Blanco could help fortify the starting rotation down the stretch in lieu of outside additions. Blanco struggled enough to lose his starting job. Wesneski, who acknowledged uncertainty about how he would fare in his return from surgery, did provide critical reinforcement.

Ironically, the pair combined to cover all nine innings in game 161, positioning the Astros as well as they could for Sunday. Aside from Wesneski, "everyone" on the pitching staff will be available, Espada said.

"That's exactly what we needed - able to reset our bullpen and go into the last game of the season in really good shape," Espada said. "But it started with Wesneski. Set the tone early, ton of strikes, really, really good. That's exactly what we needed. And we find ourselves in a really good spot for tomorrow."

articles.body: Naman Dhir makes his ODI debut for India after captain Shubman Gill won the toss and elected to bowl first against West Indies in the opening ODI of the series at the Greenfield International Stadium in Thiruvananthapuram on Sunday.Dhir has been handed his maiden ODI cap as India look to begin the three-match series with a win. The Indian team has also included Gurnoor Brar, while Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Ruturaj Gaikwad and KL Rahul feature in the playing XI.Gill explained that India preferred to chase on what appeared to be a decent batting surface."We're gonna bowl first, looks like a decent surface. Will come better under the lights, so want to chase. We have got a decent combination, four bowlers and two allrounders. 20-odd matches to go for the World Cup, so good for us to test the combination," Gill said after winning the toss.West Indies captain Shai Hope also said his side would have preferred to bowl first, expecting the surface to improve under lights."We are gonna bowl first, looks like a decent surface. Will come better under the lights, so want to chase," Hope said.India vs West Indies 1st ODI: Playing XIsIndia Playing XI: Rohit Sharma, Shubman Gill (c), Virat Kohli, Ruturaj Gaikwad, KL Rahul (w), Naman Dhir, Ravindra Jadeja, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Gurnoor Brar, Kuldeep Yadav, Prasidh KrishnaWest Indies Playing XI: John Campbell, Justin Greaves, Keacy Carty, Shai Hope (w/c), Amir Jangoo, Jewel Andrew, Roston Chase, Matthew Forde, Gudakesh Motie, Alzarri Joseph, Jayden SealesIndia opt to bowl despite batting-friendly pitchThe pitch report suggested that conditions could favour the batters at the Greenfield International Stadium. articles.title: Virender Sehwag’s Gen Z kids feared his Rise And Fall 2 hosting debut would hurt his image, but he chose to try something new
articles.summary: Virender Sehwag is known for his fearless approach to cricket, but his latest career move reportedly left his Gen Z children less than convinced.
articles.body: Virender Sehwag is known for his fearless approach to cricket, but his latest career move reportedly left his Gen Z children less than convinced. The former India cricketer has stepped into a new role as the host of the reality show Rise And Fall Season 2, marking his first stint as a reality show host. In an exclusive conversation with NDTV, Sehwag revealed that his sons, Aryavir and Vedant, questioned his decision to take up the show because they were concerned about the arguments and confrontations that are part of reality television. They feared the format could affect their father's public image and expose him to viewer criticism. “They were upset, they said, ‘Papa, why are you doing this?’ Because these shows will have fights and arguments. What will you do there? Your image will be spoiled. People will abuse you,” Sehwag recalled. Rather than allowing their concerns to stop him, Sehwag saw the programme as an opportunity to explore a completely different side of his career.Why Sehwag decided to leave the cricket comfort zoneAfter years of appearing as a cricket commentator and participating in cricket-focused television programmes, Sehwag said he wanted to experiment with something different. “So, I said, it’s okay, we can try something new. I have done a lot of cricket commentary, I have done a lot of cricket shows. Now perhaps we can try this and see how this show goes,” he said. The former cricketer also explained to his children that hosting a reality show does not necessarily mean becoming part of every confrontation. If contestants argue, he said, his responsibility would be to step in and attempt to handle the situation. “And I said, if people fight, then it is my job to explain things to them, right? So I can try doing that,” Sehwag said.His explanation, however, did not completely convince his children. “They said, ‘Okay, okay, but this is not right.’ So, they are not convinced,” he added. Their reaction highlights an interesting reversal in the usual parent-child dynamic. Instead of a parent worrying about a child's career choice, Sehwag found himself explaining a professional decision to his sons, who were concerned about how public criticism might affect him.What to expect from Rise And Fall Season 2Rise and Fall Season 2 marks a significant change in the show's hosting lineup, with Sehwag taking over from Ashneer Grover. NDTV previously reported that the season would feature 15 contestants divided into two groups, Rulers and Workers, with the format built around strategy, power shifts, alliances and competition. The official Prime Video listing describes the second season as a game in which Rulers control the game while Workers compete to rise to the top. Contestants face challenges, form alliances and deal with betrayals and votes as their positions change throughout the competition. The second season premiered on September 26, 2026, on Prime Video. The confirmed lineup includes names such as Priyanka Chahar Choudhary, Tej Pratap Yadav, Raj Grover and Kajal Raghwani, among others.For Sehwag, the move represents a departure from the world in which audiences have known him for years. He built his reputation as an aggressive opening batter and later became a familiar voice in cricket commentary. Reality television, by contrast, places the host in the middle of arguments, personalities, alliances and unpredictable moments. That difference may be exactly what Sehwag finds appealing. His children's concerns also reflect the reality of taking on a highly visible entertainment role. A reality show can expose a host to criticism that is very different from the scrutiny associated with sport. Sehwag, however, appears willing to accept that uncertainty. For now, his approach is straightforward: after spending years discussing cricket, he wants to see whether he can take on a new challenge. And while his sons may still be “not convinced”, Sehwag has decided to give this new innings a chance.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: England vs Sri Lanka: Tom Banton sets up huge win in series decider
articles.summary: Tom Banton delivers on all of his potential by crashing a brilliant first international century as England wrapped up their summer with an ODI series win over Sri Lanka.
articles.body:
Third Metro Bank one-day international, Kia Oval

England 355-7 (50 overs): Banton 126, Brook 77, Cox 76

Sri Lanka 132 (29.1 overs): Kusal 35; Dawson 3-26

Tom Banton delivered on all of his potential by crashing a brilliant first international century as England wrapped up their summer with an ODI series win over Sri Lanka.

The 27-year-old right-hander was once the rising star of English cricket when handed a debut in 2019 but afterwards fell out of love with the game after losing his way.

After reaching his hundred in 95 balls in the third one-day international at The Oval, he stood with arms wide and looked to the sky - all of that disappointment seemingly behind him.

"My fiance, Lilly, was here and all of her family," Banton said.

"Unfortunately, my mum, dad and brother weren't here because whenever my mum seems to come I don't do that well.

"Bless her, she is not banned from coming, but she avoids coming now."

The opener went on to make 126 from 105 deliveries, perfectly countering tricky early conditions - conditions in which Joe Root struggled uncharacteristically for 18 from 37 balls - and going on to share an increasingly aggressive stand of 150 in 117 balls with captain Harry Brook.

"To score a hundred for England is just the best feeling on earth," Banton said. "I don't think anything is going to beat it."

Brook made 77 and Jordan Cox, picked in the place of the injured Jos Buttler, added a 52-ball 76 to lift England to 355-7.

That always appeared a match-winning total on a surface offering bounce for the pace bowlers and turn for the spinners.

Sri Lanka crumbled to 132 all out in 29.1 overs, giving England a 223-run win and their biggest ODI victory against the tourists.

It meant England signed off their summer, one that included off-field issues, the end of Bazball, Ben Stokes' retirement and Root's surprise return as Test skipper, with a fifth successive series win amid the madness across formats.

England thrash Sri Lanka by 223 runs to win ODI series - reaction, analysis & clips

Banton's success is heartwarming. When, fresh out of Second XI cricket, he made his debut as a 20-year-old in 2019 he was seen as England's next big thing.

He was in the same England Under-19 team as Brook but, rather than the Yorkshireman who is now captain, it was the Somerset product who was given the opportunity when Eoin Morgan's World Cup-winning side needed a fresh face on its journey forward.

Tougher times followed, resulting in almost five years out of the 50-over side and only occasional T20 appearances.

During that time Kevin Pietersen, now an England mentor, said Banton "has all the talent but, at the moment, he is wasting it".

It was comparisons to Pietersen which Banton struggled with. Last week, Banton said remains "in awe" of the iconic England batter.

With thrilling reverse sweeps here, he showed the invention that drew those comparisons. He was also vicious on the pull, hit classically through the covers and, when Ben Duckett was bowled in the second over and Root faced 13 dot balls in a row, did not panic.

By the time he was dismissed he had hit 16 fours and five sixes.

When he walked off he turned and raised his bat amid a standing ovation from The Oval crowd – as Pietersen famously did 21 years ago.

Banton only has the opportunity as opener here because of Jacob Bethell's injury.

He may find himself out of the XI when England begin a tri-series in Pakistan - a series that also involves Sri Lanka - on 20 October.

The tourists, impressive in setting up this decider on Thursday, were poor here. They had already dropped Root before he was dismissed and wicketkeeper and captain Kusal Mendis spilled a thick edge when Brook had seven.

Afterwards the England captain started slowly but he kicked it into life from a position of 108-2 after 25 overs.

Also encouraging was the performance of Cox, whose knock also built on a slow start and followed an impressive run in the Test side against Pakistan.

Sonny Baker, recalled for his second ODI in place of Josh Tongue, nicked off Pathum Nissanka with a quick, swinging and rising delivery two balls into the second over, after which Sri Lanka did not recover. Left-arm spinner Liam Dawson also repaid the faith for his inclusion over Rehan Ahmed with figures of 3-26.

This summer has provided so many issues for England, including the end of Brendon McCullum's reign as Test coach.

Still his ODI side now has momentum - a third series win a row - as it builds towards next year's World Cup. Series in Pakistan, Australia and South Africa are to come this winter.

articles.title: South Africa v Australia: David Miller and Temba Bavuma hit centuries as Proteas win series
articles.summary: David Miller and Temba Bavuma's sublime centuries set up South Africa's 32-run win over Australia in a high-scoring second ODI in Johannesburg.
articles.body:
South Africa 365-9 (50 overs): Miller 142 (93); Edwards 5-67

Australia 333 (49.5 overs): Marsh 84 (53); Williams 3-54

Temba Bavuma and David Miller struck sublime centuries as South Africa beat Australia by 32 runs in the second one-day international to win the series with a game to spare.

The Proteas posted an imposing 365-9 at the Wanderers in Johannesburg, with Miller smashing 142 off 93 balls and captain Bavuma made a more measured 103 from 116.

The pair added 156 for the fourth wicket to lead an impressive recovery after Aiden Markram was dismissed from the first ball of the game, and fellow opener Quinton de Kock also fell cheaply for 15.

Bavuma reached his century from 112 balls before he holed out off Jack Edwards, but Miller continued to pummel his way to a 73-ball ton and combined with the Jansen twins, Marco and Duan, to take South Africa beyond the 350 mark.

Miller's incredible knock included 12 fours and nine sixes as he capitalised on an Australia attack that was struggling after seamer Nathan Ellis' side strain meant he could only bowl four overs, though Edwards finished with five wickets in just his second ODI outing.

Australia were faced with their record ODI chase and started strongly with a stand of 130 from the destructive opening partnership of Travis Head and Mitchell Marsh.

But neither could kick on in the manner of Bavuma or Miller, and South Africa chipped away with regular middle-order wickets after both openers fell for 84.

All-rounder Xavier Bartlett kept Australia in contention with a sensational 26-ball fifty, but he was pinned lbw by a cracking Lizaad Williams yorker to leave 44 required off the last 14 balls and they fell 32 runs short, bowled out for 333.

The series concludes at Potchefstroom on Wednesday and is followed by three Tests.

articles.title: 1st ODI: Virat Kohli, Shubman Gill centuries power India to emphatic 8-wicket win over West Indies
articles.summary: THIRUVANANTHAPURAM: Virat Kohli brought up his record 55th ODI century with an emphatic six, marching past 15,000 runs in this format.
articles.body: THIRUVANANTHAPURAM: Virat Kohli brought up his record 55th ODI century with an emphatic six, marching past 15,000 runs in this format. India captain Shubman Gill also looked imperious, as he reached his 10th ODI hundred by unfurling his signature cuts and drives. Between them, India cantered to an 8-wicket win here at the Greenfield International Stadium in a chase that never once felt like a contest.A brilliant opening salvo from Rohit Sharma, whose 35-ball 32 laid the foundation for India’s pursuit, as the hosts eased past the 295-run target in 41.4 overs against a lacklustre West Indies bowling attack. India’s insouciance with the bat came after a clinical display from Kuldeep Yadav, his wrist-spin ripping through the West Indies middle-order with a four-wicket haul. This match was a lesson in class, distance and everything in between.Gill and Kohli put together a 151-run stand for the second wicket that had the Thiruvananthapuram crowd on its feet, and for a while it looked like the two of them would see the chase home between them. Cramps and fatigue got the better of Gill, as he eventually walked off, his 110 off 108 balls, with 13 fours and a six, a knock that had class written through it. Kohli, still chasing down whatever he considers “unfinished business” before the 2027 World Cup, was unbeaten on a scarcely believable 88-ball 139 in the end, his tenth ODI ton against the West Indies.West Indies didn’t have much to show for in the afternoon, but they did have Justin Greaves. Asked to bat first, the visitors leaned almost entirely on their opener, who cracked a maiden ODI hundred, 101 off 108 balls, to drag the visitors to 295/7. He put on 135 for the first wicket with John Campbell, who chipped in with a breezy 62 off 60, and that stand alone was worth the price of admission: West Indies’ first century opening partnership in ODIs in two years.Just when the West Indies looked like running away with the game, Kuldeep spun a web with figures of 10-1-40-4. It was a tour-de-force performance by India’s virtuoso chinaman bowler who was playing a different contest to the rest of his teammates.After a string of wide deliveries that left West Indies batter John Campbell visibly tetchy, Kuldeep dropped one full and straight at the stumps. On cue, Campbell got provoked and went for a mistimed sweep that was picked up by Prasidh Krishna at backward square-leg. Kuldeep then conned West Indies captain Shai Hope with drift, eliciting a leading edge that ballooned towards Ravindra Jadeja at cover.Kuldeep’s most telling blow was the manner in which he dismissed opener Justin Greaves, who was trapped lbw after missing a sweep against a ball on a length on leg stump. Greaves’ departure set jitters in the visitors’ dressing room, and on the next delivery, the Kanpur spinner bamboozled Jewel Andrew with a googly to prise his fourth scalp.Kuldeep’s timely blows meant the West Indies would lose their momentum in the middle overs, capping a redemption for the 31-year-old, who endured a tepid Sri Lanka Test series. articles.title: England vs Sri Lanka: Tom Banton notches maiden ODI century as Harry Brook's side secure series victory after tourists collapse
articles.summary: England secured a 2-1 ODI series victory over Sri Lanka in the third ODI at the Oval after Tom Banton notched an imperious 126 off 105 balls; Jordan Cox and Harry Brook notched fifties on the way to England's 356; Pavan Rathnayake's run-out dismissal caused confusion
articles.body:
Banton top scored with his career-best but was aided by sizeable contributions by skipper Harry Brook (77 off 66) and the in-form Jordan Cox (76 off 52) as the batting side set the tourists a mammoth target of 356 after their 50 overs, with Dilhara Fernando (3-52) the pick of the bowlers - albeit with two of his wickets coming with the final two balls of the innings.

That target loomed even larger over Sri Lanka's innings when Sonny Baker nicked off Pathum Nissanka (1) for his maiden ODI wicket with just the eighth ball of their innings.

From there the wickets started to tumble for Sri Lanka who - despite the best efforts of captain Kusal Mendis (35 off 26) - went from 36-1 to 82-6 in just 10 overs, including the confusing run-out dismissal of Pavan Rathnayake (18), which was still given as out despite Jordan Cox taking the bails off before Archer's direct-hit throw dismantled the stumps.

The impressive bowling of Liam Dawson (3-17) and Gus Atkinson (2-26) then ensured Sri Lanka's tail went out with a 50-run whimper, handing England the series victory and marking a successful end of the home summer for Brendon McCullum's side after 12 wins in 14 white-ball games.

Banton brilliance headlines complete England performance

Despite England's eventual victory, it took just eight balls for Sri Lanka to take their first wicket as Ben Duckett (0) was clean bowled by Dilshan Madushanka (1-49), before Joe Root was dismissed by Janith Liyanage in an uncharacteristically stiff cameo that saw him notch just 18 off 37 balls.

It was then the partnership of Brook and player-of-the-match Banton that made the difference for England, putting on 150 runs in a lucrative partnership that was eventually ended when the former was caught on the boundary by Dunith Wellalage.

Banton's majestic innings - featuring 21 boundaries and including five sixes - came to a conclusion when his effort to hit a sixth maximum was caught by Malinga at long-on.

But England were not done there - alongside Will Jacks (25 off 21), Cox spearheaded a late flurry of runs, notching his half-century off 42 balls before Fernando took his and Dawson's wickets with the final two balls of the 49th over, leaving England in the ascendancy after posting a formidable score of 355-7.

Sri Lanka were immediately left reeling after Baker's early wicket and found it difficult to recover, with no batter scoring above 20 bar their captain Mendis, with their woes being immediately compounded by the controversial run out of Pavan Rathnayake.

Cox appeared to have made a mishap after taking the bails off the stumps before he was in control of the ball, but - after a near five-minute period of discussion involving both umpires and players - Archer's direct-hit throw uprooting the stump was ruled legitimate.

His dismissal was followed by that of Charith Asalanka and Wellalage within the next eight balls, leaving Sri Lanka on the brink of defeat at 82-6 with no recognised batters left, before the excellent work of Dawson - taking three of the last four Sri Lanka wickets - ensured England's dominant victory was confirmed with 21.5 overs to spare.

Brook: That was a near-perfect performance

England captain Harry Brook, speaking to Sky Sports:

"I thought that was a near-perfect performance there - I thought everyone chipped in and it was an exceptional win.

"There was some tough periods, but I thought the patience we showed, it was exceptional.

"We want to be able to adapt to conditions every game. Every surface has been slightly different. That is the side we want to be - we want to win when they are not in our favour and when they are, we want to nail sides.

"We are building towards a squad where someone can come into roles and fill it exceptionally well. We are building to a strong squad and I have full trust in anyone who comes in."

"We struggled with the batting and then we made some mistakes in the field, including me.

"I think we played good cricket in the second ODI and when go to Pakistan after this, we need to be better.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Virat Kohli reached another major ODI milestone on Sunday, but the star batter made it clear that records and numbers have never been his main focus.Kohli became only the second batter after Sachin Tendulkar to complete 15,000 ODI runs. He also hit his record-extending 55th ODI century as India beat West Indies by eight wickets in the first ODI.Kohli wants to keep pushing himselfKohli said his priority has always been to understand the situation and do what the team needs."My focus has never really been on these milestones, so to say. It's just understanding the situation along the course of just doing the job for the team, (the) achievements come along," Kohli told the broadcaster after the match.Kohli smashed nine sixes and 10 fours to remain unbeaten on 139 off 88 balls. India scored 300 for two in 41.4 overs while chasing West Indies' 295 for seven."Obviously, I feel very grateful and very blessed to be in this position for having played for so long. Just keeping my head down, working hard and thanking God for everything that I've been blessed with and the opportunities that I've got in my life to be where I am," Kohli said."We have a very blessed life and a blessed journey because so many people want to be here, but we get to be the lucky ones, so we better put our head down and just work hard every day of our lives," he added.A new challenge at this stageKohli said becoming more aggressive with the bat and playing at a higher gear has been a challenge for him at this stage of his career."… just the understanding of your game, firstly. Also, at the stage that I'm at, just keeping myself physically very fit because the game's more or less in the mind. I've never been a guy who practised a lot even when I was playing all three formats as you know," he replied to a query from former India coach Ravi Shastri."For me it's about about staying mentally fresh, staying in the present moment and just expressing myself really out there to play in a certain way, get used to this template more often.""I got a challenge at this stage of my career to kind of up the ante and play a gear or two higher and yeah, that was exciting for me to work on."He continued, "Again, it excites you when you have to unlock a new version at this stage of your career, which will eventually help any team that you play for, be it playing for India or in the IPL. It's really helped me a lot to play with a free mind and I think that's what's working for me."Fitness helps him play with a free mindKohli also spoke about the role of fitness in his batting and how it helps him visualise his game."I think to follow a free mind, you need a fit body so for me, it works the other way around. I stay physically fit and then I'm able to visualise the game in the way that I want to play, which allows me the best chance to go out there and execute in the way that I did tonight," he said.He also stressed the importance of remembering the journey that brought him to this stage."I think the only thing we need to do is just look back once and where we came from. That's something that we tend to forget when we are caught up with the hustle of the world and the positions we get into with so much attention and fame and so much love from the fans" he said."It can be very easy to forget where you came from. But just looking back at the journey from when you started as a child just makes you feel grateful."Kohli added, "I enjoy each and every minute that I'm out there playing for India because I understand that, as I said I could have been a possibility that I wouldn't be standing here. I wouldn't have played for India at all."World Cup goal is clearThe 37-year-old said playing only one format for India has also given him clarity about what he wants to achieve."We are a year away from the World Cup. I know what my goal is and it's pretty clear for me that whatever games we get, I just need to keep working on different aspects of the game, keep myself physically fit, challenge myself to be out there.""… run from boundary to boundary in the last 15 overs if I can, field in the inner ring, show intensity. If I keep ticking all those boxes, I've got some time left to play in this format as well.""So when I get an opportunity, I feel happy rather than feeling anxiety or pressure to make the most of it. I just want to express myself and play my game. As I said, I promised myself I'm going to play positively because I can.""I'm going to continue to play like that but not be reckless. articles.title: Dodgers recall Bobby Miller with Blake Treinen on injured list
articles.summary: One last transaction on the final day of the regular season, with Blake Treinen placed on the 15-day injured list with right shoulder inflammation one day af...
articles.body:
One last transaction on the final day of the regular season, with Blake Treinen placed on the 15-day injured list with right shoulder inflammation one day after suffering the injury while warming up in the bullpen at Oracle Park in San Francisco . Bobby Miller was recalled from the Triple-A champion Oklahoma City Comets to help fill innings for the Dodgers in Game No. 162 against the Giants on Sunday.

Treinen was warming up in the top of the seventh inning but suddenly stopped, feeling something in his shoulder. Instead, Brock Stewart entered the game in the bottom of the inning having not warmed up at all.

"I don't know if it was a complete blowout. But really unfortunate," manager Dave Roberts told reporters at Oracle Park in San Francisco on Saturday . "We're going to get imaging, obviously it's an IL, his season's over."

Miller returns to the Dodgers having thrown scoreless innings for Oklahoma City in Games 1 and 3 of the Pacific Coast League championship series on Tuesday and Thursday. He did not pitch in Saturday's Triple-A championship game in Las Vegas.

Miller's two appearance with the Dodgers this season have been three innings and 2 1/3 innings, and the Dodgers might need multiple innings for Sunday's bullpen game.

His activation gives the Dodgers 10 relievers on the active roster, but closer Tanner Scott pitched on both Friday and Saturday, so he's likely unavailable on Sunday. The Dodgers used five relievers for one inning apiece after Blake Snell 's four-inning tuneup on Saturday.

If Evan Phillips pitches on Sunday, it will make three appearances in four days for him, not out of the question, but perhaps something the Dodgers want to avoid in a game with literally no stakes. Same for Kris Bubic , who pitched an inning on Saturday and hasn't pitched on back-to-back days this year.

So the Dodgers might have seven relievers to cover the nine innings on Sunday. Miller can give them multiple innings, as can Justin Wrobleski , who last pitched two-thirds of an inning on Thursday, and perhaps Roki Sasaki , who last pitched Friday.

Jack Dreyer is the first pitcher for the Dodgers on Sunday, making his 67th appearance of the season, tying his total from his 2025 rookie campaign.

articles.title: Australia suffer ODI series defeat to South Africa as David Miller and Temba Bavuma both hit hundreds
articles.summary: David Miller (142 off 93 balls) and Temba Bavuma (103 off 116) each hit hundreds as South Africa posted 365-9, before bowling Australia out for 333; watch the third and final ODI on Wednesday, live on Sky Sports Cricket from 12pm (first ball 12.30pm)
articles.body:
David Miller (142 off 93 balls) and Temba Bavuma (103 off 116) each smashed centuries for South Africa as they set the visitors a massive 366-run target after being inserted at the toss.

Australia looked well placed early on in their reply, with openers Mitch Marsh (84 off 53) and ​Travis Head (85 off 76) setting the tone by blazing the bowling to all parts.

But ultimately the tourists' middle-order batting issues and struggles against spin were again laid bare. From 191-2 in the 25th over, they added only 62 for the loss of four wickets in the next 15 and a bit overs to stumble to 253-6.

That left Australia needing another 113 runs to win from the final 10 overs and, despite a late counter-punch from Xavier Bartlett (50 off 28), they'd eventually be bowled out for 333 in the final over.

Keshav Maharaj took 2-54, Bjorn Fortuin 2-70 and Aiden Markram 1-55 among the Proteas' spin options. Seamer Lizaad Williams 3-54 and Marco Jansen 2-53.

"It's certainly an area where we need to improve and we're well aware of that," Australia captain ‌Marsh said. "I thought we set up our innings really well in both games but we haven't been able to execute during those middle ‌phases.

"It's a great learning curve, especially for some of our younger players. But you also have to give South Africa full credit for the way they've bowled during those periods."

Miller's eighth ODI ton - containing 12 fours and nine sixes - and captain Bavuma's sixth had helped South Africa to a score of 365-9 from their 50 overs.

Jack Edwards, playing in only his second ODI, grabbed 5-67 and Josh Hazlewood, who dismissed Aiden Markram off the first ball for a golden duck, took 3-70.

Australia, who haven't won a bilateral ODI series against South Africa since 2014, will look for a consolation win in the last game in Potchefstroom on Wednesday. They've lost 19 of their last 25 ODIs against their hosts.

"It was another really good ⁠all-round team performance," Bavuma said. "It started with the bat. ​Conditions were a little tricky up front but we managed to get through ​that period and build towards a good total.

"David played an unbelievable innings and then the bowlers did their job as well."

articles.title: India vs West Indies: Virat Kohli joins Sachin Tendulkar in passing 15,000 ODI runs as his 55th ton fires India to victory
articles.summary: Virat Kohli smashed an unbeaten 139 off 88 balls, including 10 fours and nine sixes, as India successfully chased down 296 in just 41.4 overs to beat West Indies by eight wickets in first ODI; the 37-year-old now only plays ODI cricket internationally after retiring from Tests and T20Is
articles.body:
India's star batter - who now only plays this format in international cricket - smashed an unbeaten 139 off 88 balls, including 10 fours and nine sixes, as India successfully chased down 296 in just 41.4 overs.

In doing so, the 37-year-old also became only the second batter after Sachin Tendulkar (18,426) to pass 15,000 runs in ODIs.

"My focus has never been on milestones. Just looking back at the start of my journey, it makes me feel very grateful," Kohli said. "I enjoy each and every minute that I am out there playing for India, and I am able to do the job for my team. As a cricketer, this is all I could dream of."

Skipper Shubman Gill also notched a century, scoring 110 off 108 deliveries as India registered an easy win - clinched with a Kohli six - to go 1-0 up in the three-match series.

Earlier, West Indies had posted 295-7 from their 50 overs after being put into bat. Opener Justin Greaves (101 off 108) scored his maiden ODI ton, sharing in an impressive 135-run opening partnership with John Campbell (62 off 60) inside the first 20 overs.

Wrist spinner Kuldeep Yadav (4-40) ultimately accounted for both as he wreaked havoc in the middle overs to see West Indies reduced to 198-5 by the 36th.

Amir Jangoo's unbeaten 58 off 43 balls helped revive the innings, but their target of 296 ultimately proved an under-par one on a batter-friendly pitch.

It was a quick-fire chase for India as openers Gill and Rohit Sharma added 74 off 72 balls, Sharma scoring 32 off 35 before he fell to Alzarri Joseph (1-81) in the 12th over.

Kohli came to the crease and promptly eased his way to fifty in only 40 balls, hitting the 15,000-milestone on the way - the fastest to do it at 303 innings, compared to Tendulkar's 377.

He and Gill put on 151 off 132 balls for the second wicket before the captain departed against the run of play to Roston Chase (1-64) in the 34th over.

But Kohli cruised to a 74-ball hundred, before finishing the game in style with 8.2 overs to spare. Kohli's nine sixes were his most in an ODI innings.

Guwahati and Chandigarh will host the second and third ODIs on Wednesday and Saturday, followed by a five-match T20 series starting on October 6.

articles.title: Dodgers finish with 100 wins, turn their attention to October
articles.summary: SAN FRANCISCO — The Dodgers saved one last bit of drama for the final game of the regular season.
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO — The Dodgers saved one last bit of drama for the final game of the regular season.

Locked in a 1-1 game with the Giants entering the 10th inning, the Dodgers finally broke through when Alex Call delivered the go-ahead RBI single, scoring the run that put the Dodgers in front for good.

Then Andy Pages made sure there would be no comeback.

Pages followed with his 23rd home run of the season, a three-run shot that turned a one-run game into a 5-1 victory and sent the Dodgers into October with a flourish.

The Dodgers finish the regular season 100-62, their first 100-win season since 2023 and the sixth 100-win campaign of Dave Roberts' managerial tenure. It is the 12th 100-win season in franchise history.

The Dodgers finished September with an 18-7 record, pushing through the final month to reach the century mark and complete a sweep of the Giants in the final three games of the regular season.

Pages finished the night with four RBI and 85 for the season. Tommy Edman went 2-for-3, while Max Muncy reached base four times with two hits and two walks.

But it was Call who started the decisive rally.

His 20th RBI of the season gave the Dodgers a 2-1 lead in the 10th. Pages then delivered the knockout blow.

The pitching staff got there through another bullpen game, one that proved efficient enough to secure the victory and complete the sweep.

Jack Dreyer opened the game and threw 32 pitches, 22 for strikes, across two innings. He allowed one earned run on two hits while striking out two and finished his season with a 3.20 ERA.

Justin Wrobleski followed with two scoreless innings before Roki Sasaki worked a clean fifth, retiring all three hitters he faced.

Edwin Díaz added another scoreless inning on 11 pitches. Since returning from the injured list, Díaz has made five appearances and thrown five scoreless innings, striking out nine while walking one and allowing just one hit.

Sep 27, 2026; San Francisco, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Bobby Miller (28) delivers against the San Francisco Giants during the seventh inning at Oracle Park.

Then Bobby Miller took over and delivered perhaps the biggest bullpen performance of the afternoon, striking out five across two scoreless innings.

It was enough to get the Dodgers to the finish line.

Now comes the pause before the games that matter most.

The Dodgers will have five days off before hosting Game 1 of the National League Division Series at Uniqlo Field at Dodger Stadium next Saturday. Their opponent will be the winner of the Phillies-Braves series.

For a team that has spent the final month building toward this moment, the regular season is officially over.

The record is 100-62. And the Dodgers are counting down to their next 11 victories.

"We are gonna be ready for 11 more games, and hopefully we can win another championship," Teoscar Hernández said.

Freddie Freeman put it even more simply.

articles.title: Kevin Pietersen promises to challenge Brendon McCullum as England white-ball head coach eyes world No 1 ranking
articles.summary: England's new white-ball specialist mentor Kevin Pietersen tells Sky Sports Cricket: "There are times when Harry Brook stands at the wicket and he goes, 'This is too easy'" but adds: "I will never in my life try and take the flair and that genius out of him"
articles.body:
Since retiring as a player in 2018, Pietersen has, at times, been an outspoken critic of the England setup, including when accusing the white-ball team of inadequate preparation on a tour of India last January after McCullum had just taken over.

Pietersen's work with England began with a 3-0 T20 series whitewash of Sri Lanka, before the hosts then also clinched a 2-1 ODI series success over the same side on Sunday. His role with the team will continue through to the 2027 50-over World Cup in just over a year's time.

"Brendon, when he first called me, I thought I was in trouble because I'd said something, but he said this exact point: 'I'd like you to come in and challenge me,'" Pietersen told Sky Sports Cricket ahead of England's series-clinching 223-run win over Sri Lanka at The Oval .

"He's since said to me: 'I absolutely love the fact that you are inside the rooms and you are picking on things that can make the players better.'

"And at the end of the day, if we can't do that as a coach, try and challenge players to be the best versions of themselves, I think we're letting them down because these guys are too good."

Pietersen added on his coaching approach: "No stone unturned. There are a few things I don't like. There are many things that I do like, and I think if we can get that balance right, I think that these guys are going to be very, very good.

"That messaging and that constant drive to be the best version of themselves is something that we're drilling down on.

"It's been a brilliant period to understand what actually is happening inside that dressing room. There's a crazy amount of talent up there."

McCullum was similarly bullish about his hopes for the 50-over side, specifically with a World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia in a year's time.

The T20 team have won 22 of their past 25 completed T20 internationals since the start of last summer, assuming the No 1 spot in the world rankings as a result, and McCullum wants similar for the ODI team, currently sixth in the standings.

"I've also found that with a little bit of extra time, I've been able to drill down on some aspects of where you want to take this team and how you want to shape it," McCullum, who was removed as England Test coach earlier this summer, told Sky Sports Cricket .

"At the time, I was very comfortable doing it all [Test and white-ball jobs]. Change happens and my focus now is on how to make this side the best white-ball team in the world.

"We're not there yet. We've got a lot of growth within us and a lot of improvement to make, but there's a determination within the dressing room to be the best team in the world.

"I want us to become the strongest, fastest and most robust cricket teams in the world, one that can play at a high-octane speed.

"The performance we saw today [against Sri Lanka] was brilliant. You go to a World Cup, you got to do it time and time and time again over a long period of time. So that'll be a focus for us over the next little while.

Pietersen: Brook finds game 'too easy' at times

McCullum and Pietersen also both singled out white-ball captain Harry Brook, specifically, for praise.

Brook, despite being vice-captain, was overlooked for the Test captaincy in favour of Joe Root when Ben Stokes retired, but continues to impress in the white-ball role.

"I think he's an outstanding tactician, he's growing as a leader and maturing as a person - and doing it at rapid speed," McCullum said.

"Tactically he's outstanding; he's very much the leader of the side. The boys respect him immensely, and not just for his cricket brain but the way he creates the right environment.

"It's like a group of mates playing together, which is which is plain to see when when you watch them play out in the middle."

With the bat against Sri Lanka, Brook notched two half-centuries in the ODI series to go with a 42-ball hundred - England's joint-second-fastest - in the opening T20I.

That innings saw Brook hailed as an "absolute freak" by Ben Stokes, who took to social media to say that, in his opinion, the Yorkshireman's ability outstrips that of Pietersen.

But as well as being capable of achieving the incredible, both Brook and Pietersen have had their share of percieved 'brain fade' moments.

Addressing that similarity, Pietersen said: "Looking back at my career, the brain fade moments happen because sometimes you see the game differently. And that's what the fan and the spectator needs to understand... Harry Brook is a player that sees the game differently.

"There are times when Harry Brook stands at the wicket and he goes, 'This is too easy.'

"The one thing that I'm working really hard with Brooky, and will continue to work hard on, is just being better at assessing game situations.

"I will never in my life try and take the flair and that genius out of him."

Second T20 (Cardiff) - England won by six wickets

Third T20 (Old Trafford) - England won by eight wickets

First ODI (Durham) - England won by 89 runs
